questions.q: What is an ansatz in the context of VQE?
options: The fixed, parameterized circuit structure used to prepare trial states, whose tunable parameters are searched over classically
The final measured ground state energy of a Hamiltonian
A classical-only algorithm with no quantum circuit involved
The Hamiltonian matrix itself, written in Pauli operator form
questions.explain: An ansatz is the chosen circuit layout (fixed in advance) used to prepare trial states |psi(theta)>; only its numerical parameters theta are adjusted during optimization.

questions.q: For a single-qubit R_y(theta) rotation applied to |0>, what is the resulting Pauli-Z expectation value as a function of theta?
options: <Z> = sin(theta)
<Z> = cos(theta)
<Z> = theta
<Z> = 1 for all theta
questions.explain: The R_y(theta) ansatz gives <Z> = cos(theta), verified directly at theta=0 (1.0), theta=pi/2 (0.0), and theta=pi (-1.0), sweeping continuously across the entire possible range of Z-expectation values.

questions.q: What is the key structural difference between a hardware-efficient ansatz and a chemistry-inspired (UCC/UCCSD) ansatz?
options: Hardware-efficient ansätze use gates chosen for cheap, accurate execution on specific hardware; UCC ansätze use gates motivated by physical electron-excitation behavior, often needing fewer parameters for molecules but deeper circuits
Hardware-efficient ansätze never use any single-qubit gates
UCC ansätze cannot be implemented on any real quantum hardware
There is no meaningful difference; the two names refer to the same circuit design
questions.explain: Hardware-efficient ansätze prioritize low hardware error using native gates, while UCC/UCCSD ansätze encode physical chemistry insight about electron excitations, typically trading circuit depth for fewer needed parameters on molecular problems.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say the ansatz you choose directly limits what ground energy VQE can possibly find?
options: Because if the true ground state cannot be expressed by any setting of the ansatz's parameters, the best achievable result is the closest representable state, which by the variational principle has energy strictly above the true E_0
Because every ansatz, regardless of structure, can always reach the exact true ground state
Because the ansatz only affects how fast the circuit runs, never what states it can represent
Because classical optimizers can bypass the ansatz entirely and search all possible quantum states directly
questions.explain: The ansatz defines the entire set of states VQE can ever reach; by the variational principle (Lesson 11), any state outside that reachable set being the true ground state means VQE can only approach it from above via the closest representable state.

questions.q: What is the central 'expressiveness-vs-trainability' tradeoff in ansatz design?
options: More parameters and richer structure can represent a wider range of states (including closer approximations to the true ground state), but also create a harder, higher-dimensional classical optimization problem more prone to barren plateaus
Expressiveness and trainability always increase together with no tradeoff at all
Only hardware-efficient ansätze face any tradeoff; UCC ansätze have none
Trainability refers only to how many qubits a quantum computer physically has
questions.explain: An ansatz that's too simple can't reach a good answer regardless of optimization quality, while one that's too elaborate can represent a good answer in principle but become practically very hard to train -- exactly the tension that makes ansatz design an active research problem rather than a solved recipe.
